title: Chord finder
description: Play or type some notes to get the chord name, or type a chord symbol to get its notes.

title: Scale chords
description: Pick a tonic and any of 92 scales to see the chord on each degree: triads, sevenths, or chords stacked in fourths or seconds.

title: Key explorer
description: Click a key on the circle of fifths to get its signature, scale and chords: diatonic chords with their functions, secondary and substitute dominants with their ii, chord scales, and the related keys. Major and the three minor scales.

title: Chart reader
description: Paste a chord chart with sections, repeats, endings and D.S. al Coda to see the form as it's played, bar by bar, and read every symbol: notes, family, complexity and roman numerals in a key, with applied dominants. Transpose it and play it.

title: Scale families
description: The seven modes of the major, melodic minor, harmonic minor and other scale families, side by side, and which of them fit a chord.

title: Scale harmonizer
description: Add voices in thirds, sixths or tenths that stay in a scale to a melody, and see how consonant each interval is.

title: Voicings
description: Voice a chord progression for piano: how many voices, which tensions, who plays the bass, rootless and So What templates, drop 2 and spread. Each chord led smoothly from the one before.

title: Rhythm patterns
description: Draw a rhythm on a circle, or pick a clave or a Euclidean rhythm, and see why some rhythms recur around the world: evenness, rhythmic oddity, deepness, off-beatness and distances, from Toussaint's The Geometry of Musical Rhythm. Lay it over a meter (6/8, 2+2+3/8) to hear its pulses, and play it with drums.

title: Note patterns
description: Play arpeggios and melodic sequences over a chord progression: an arpeggio order or a cell of indexes, over each chord's voicing, its chord tones or the scale, kept in a register and put on a rhythm.
